name: Teardown Atlas — any object as an annotated exploded diagram
one_liner: Upload a photo of any object — a espresso machine, a drone, a sneaker — and get back a labelled, exploded technical diagram you can edit part-by-part and export as SVG or PNG.
problem: For curious people, teachers, hardware makers and content creators who want to explain how a thing works: today they either hunt for a patent drawing, pay an illustrator, or hand-draw in Figma/Illustrator. A multimodal model can now look at one photo, enumerate the plausible parts, and lay them out as a clean exploded view with callout labels. The tedious part this removes is the hour of tracing and labelling to produce one explainer image.
target_customer: Builders and makers on X, teachers and science communicators, hardware/product-marketing folks who need a "how it works" graphic, and newsletter writers. They hang out on X, r/engineeringporn, Hacker News and design Discords.
why_now: @jakubkrehel's /teardown agent skill (npx skills add jakubkrehel/skills, 5.1k likes on 25 Oct 2026) showed the output is now good enough to be delightful — but it lives inside an agent CLI for people who install skills. Current image models reliably emit structured SVG with text labels, so the same result can be a no-signup web page with one input box. Nothing in search surfaced a free web app that turns a photo into an *editable, labelled* exploded diagram; the nearest hits are generic "technical drawing" prompt wrappers (aifreeforever, OpenArt) that produce a flat picture with no parts you can toggle or relabel.
comparables: jakubkrehel's /teardown skill (https://x.com/jakubkrehel/status/2114379959263502712) — same output, but CLI-only, requires installing an agent skill; this is a public URL, no install, with a shareable permalink per diagram. OpenArt AI CAD Drawing Generator (https://openart.ai/generator/cad-drawing/) and aifreeforever's Technical Drawing Image Generator (https://aifreeforever.com/image-generators/technical-drawing-image-generator) — text-to-image only, raster output, no part list, no editing. Onshape exploded views (https://www.onshape.com/de/blog/repurposing-cad-models-for-marketing-sales) — needs a real CAD model. The gap: photo in, editable labelled SVG out, free, in a browser.
validation_test: Post the moka-pot and mechanical-keyboard diagrams as a single image on X with the launch copy and a link to the live page. Pass: 300+ likes and 50+ people pasting their own exploded output in replies within 48 hours. Fail: under 50 likes and fewer than 5 generated outputs shared — means it reads as "another AI image toy" and the editable-SVG angle needs to lead instead.
build_plan: Next.js + Tailwind on Vercel (the builder's TS comfort zone). Steps: 1) one drop-zone that accepts a photo or an object name; 2) one multimodal call that returns strict JSON — {part_name, function_one_liner, bbox/position, layer_order} — plus a second call that renders the exploded SVG; 3) render the SVG client-side so each part is a real <g> element: click a part to rename it, toggle its label, recolour, or hide it; 4) style presets (blueprint, patent-ink, mid-century manual, neon); 5) Export SVG / PNG and a "copy share link" that encodes the diagram JSON; 6) ship the repo public with the prompt in the README. Cut: 3D, accuracy claims, accounts, galleries, payments. Rate-limit by IP and put a "bring your own key" box for heavy users.
launch_post:
Upload a photo of anything and get an exploded technical diagram of it — every part labelled, every label editable, export as SVG.

Coffee grinder, AirPods case, a bike, your keyboard. Free, no signup, open source.
reasoning:
Tonight's bookmarks split cleanly: a cluster about agent infrastructure (Cursor Agent SDK with built-in evals, supermemory's learner-1, sriramk asking who-did-what across his personal agents, katelyn_lesse on multiagent engineering) and a cluster of delightful single-output toys (nutlope's IKEA video, nutlope's bookmark library, jakubkrehel's /teardown skill). The agent-infra cluster is where the library is already crowded — SkillProof, SkillPeek, Driftwatch, Doublecheck, Ledger and AgentGauntlet all live there — so I deliberately pushed the venture away from "watch your agents" governance, which sriramk's post would otherwise have produced as a near-repeat of Doublecheck/Ledger with a consumer coat of paint.

The lead is a build because it scores higher and fits the taste file almost exactly: one input, one striking output in seconds, no signup, open source — the roomGPT/Napkins shape. It is inspired by jakubkrehel's /teardown but is not a clone: his lives as an agent skill you install via npx in a CLI, aimed at people already running agent skills; this is a public web page with no install, and the real differentiator is that the output is a live, editable SVG — click a part, rename it, hide it, drag an explosion slider — rather than a one-shot render. Search found no free web app doing photo→editable labelled exploded diagram; the nearest things are text-to-image "technical drawing" wrappers and CAD tools. Pain is latent — nobody writes "I wish I could explode my kettle" — so what makes people notice it is the demo image itself: the launch post is the output, and one good screenshot of an exploded moka pot does the persuading. Strongest failure reason: a once-and-done toy. The narrow hedge is the editability and SVG export, which gives teachers, hardware marketers and newsletter writers a reason to return; that is also why could_grow is true (a paid tier for brands needing "how it works" graphics is visible from here).

The runner-up venture, EvalSeed, comes from the Cursor Agent SDK line "built-in evals let you measure every change." Every eval vendor (Braintrust, Langfuse, Confident AI, Promptfoo) assumes you already have a golden dataset; the repeated complaint in the search results is that writing the cases is the bottleneck and that golden sets go stale. EvalSeed attacks case authorship, not case running, and sells to the agent builder rather than the platform owner — different from AgentGauntlet, which tests whether *outside* agents can use your product, and from Driftwatch, which watches vendor surfaces. It scores 6.6 rather than higher because the incumbents are well-funded and could ship generation as a feature; the wedge has to be very narrow (Cursor Agent SDK repos specifically) to survive.
candidates_considered: 1) Exploded (build, WON) — photo to editable labelled exploded SVG; differs from the /teardown skill by being installable-free and editable. 2) EvalSeed (venture, RUNNER-UP) — generates eval cases from an agent's Markdown prompt + TS tools; attacks the authorship bottleneck the eval vendors assume away. 3) Agent attribution ledger for personal agents (from sriramk) — dropped: same core workflow as Doublecheck and Ledger in the library (record every agent write, resolve who did what), and the consumer version has no buyer with budget. 4) Messenger-broadcast compliance checker (from the Blueberry post) — dropped: the underlying practice looks like it rides Meta policy edges; not something to build a business on, and I could find no corroborating sources. 5) Cross-assistant memory wallet built on supermemory/learner-1 — dropped: Mem0 ($24M Series A per rywalker.com), Zep, Letta, Cognee and supermemory itself are all funded and shipping exactly this; the gap is closed for a solo builder. 6) "IKEA manual to talk-you-through-it steps" app (from nutlope's post) — dropped as too close to a thin re-do of the bookmark that inspired it, and the manual-PDF corpus is a licensing swamp.
research_notes: 12-call budget, 11 used. Two Web Summary calls resolved the two thinnest-but-most-promising posts: supermemory's learner-1 (it is an external memory layer with an API, not weight-level continual learning — which killed candidate 5's premise of a novel capability) and the Cursor Agent SDK (confirmed Markdown prompts, TypeScript tools, built-in evals, event replay, no published separate price — which seeded EvalSeed). Searches: prior art for agent-attribution tooling (found only enterprise-side signals — Glean release notes now tagging which assistant triggered an action, Scalekit's OAuth-for-agents writing, Cloud Security Alliance on agent audit logs — i.e. the enterprise version is already being absorbed by platforms, so I dropped the consumer version); prior art for IKEA-manual and manual-PDF apps (nothing credible, but licensing risk); prior art for exploded/technical diagram generators (only text-to-image wrappers: OpenArt, aifreeforever — no editable-SVG-from-photo tool, which is what unlocked the build); eval tooling landscape and the golden-dataset bottleneck (Braintrust, Confident AI, Langfuse, Promptfoo, Hamel Husain, Microsoft Foundry's `azd ai agent eval generate` — this last one is the clearest warning that generation is becoming a platform feature, which capped EvalSeed's gap score); memory-layer funding (Mem0 $24M Series A, supermemory $3M pre-seed — closed the memory gap). Three searches returned nothing usable (Blueberry/Messenger broadcasts, consumer multi-agent memory, UiPath Maestro governance comparables), which is itself why candidates 3 and 4 were dropped rather than reshaped: I would not assert a market I could not source.
prototype_summary: An interactive "Exploded" prototype that turns a sample photo into an editable, annotated exploded-view SVG diagram with explosion slider, part renaming/recolouring, visibility toggles, four art styles and SVG export.
